### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via COPY (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f926dfaba8e95847cd6dcbfab547a996c87834e8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b493bd58d34ce1048d13eb1cdac6d12fc6699f64` — the merge of head `7c96d5bf9a11d9091b818acede64f1c14ee224a2` into base `f926dfaba8e95847cd6dcbfab547a996c87834e8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b493bd58d34ce1048d13eb1cdac6d12fc6699f64 && git checkout b493bd58d34ce1048d13eb1cdac6d12fc6699f64
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f926dfaba8e95847cd6dcbfab547a996c87834e8 7c96d5bf9a11d9091b818acede64f1c14ee224a2 && git checkout -B drift-repro f926dfaba8e95847cd6dcbfab547a996c87834e8 && git merge --no-ff 7c96d5bf9a11d9091b818acede64f1c14ee224a2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f926dfaba8e95847cd6dcbfab547a996c87834e8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f926dfaba8e95847cd6dcbfab547a996c87834e8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5150e762807a60176067e3f04054cf3551de01aa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ask/evals/metric-selection-fallback.json + packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-next-step.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: no

Read: card #34996 (body and all 26 comments), PR #37919 (body, file list, net diff against `main`), the 61 check-runs on the head. Read and not reviewed: `dataset-term-matcher.ts` and ADR-0149 D3 on `main`. The remainder of the diff (the two test files, the changeset, `ask-skill.generated.ts`) is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Tool input and output shapes: unchanged, right.** No schema, no `packages/spec` file and no accept-set moves. `composeDatasetNextStep` gains one sentence in two places (`candidates_only` with an asked word; a left-out asked word under `one_measure`); `readTerm`, the precedence, `decision`, `terms`, `matches` and `candidates` are not touched. A measure candidate is still never selected by any text in the diff.
- **Served text that changes, in four places: right as a list.** `nextStep.note` in `en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW` and `ja-JP` (one sentence added, two question sentences conditioned on the word being the user's own); `list_datasets`' description; the MCP `initialize` selection rule; the `objectstack-ask` skill and the `GET /mcp/skill` copy generated from it. The four locales say the same thing, sentence for sentence.
- **The sentence is absent where no question is owed: right.** It is pushed only when `asked.length > 0`, so a grouping candidate, an exact match and an unknown word do not carry it.
- **The gates' verdicts are the check-runs: 41 success, 20 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending**, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (the token ratchet) and all ten `Test Core` shards among the successes.
- **Ratchet row 1875 to 1873: right.** The head's `SKILL.md` is 7516 bytes; `ceil((7516 - 27) / 4)` is 1873. The row is lowered to its measurement, no ceiling is raised.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/skills`, `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/service-analytics` matches what the diff publishes: wording only, in three packages that each ship a changed text. `Clause-②: no` holds: nothing a caller could send is refused that was accepted before, and no declared capability is narrowed. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions` in report 7217487426: none.** Its two `out_of_scope_findings` have carriers (#37921, #37923) and are not this PR's.
- **Deviation, ratchet script outside the claim's file surface: accepted.** One row lowered, shrink-only, in the same PR as the ratchet's own refusal orders.
- **Deviation, r2 measured on an uncommitted tree: noted, not judged.** This record judges the text, not the rounds.
- **Escalated to the seat: the diff says something claim amendment 7215005772 does not.** The amendment reads "call `list_datasets` once more with the user's phrase, and ask only if it still answers candidates". The diff says the opposite for a re-sent phrase with no candidate: "if that phrase matches nothing and has no candidate, the word is asked about after all". ADR-0149 D3's candidates note says of a term with no hit and no candidate that rule 4 is unchanged (the labelled fallback). Neither reading selects a measure, so the ruling that a measure candidate is asked and never chosen is kept either way; which of the two the product wants is the seat's to say, and S1 below is the same point seen from the texts.
- **ADR note: not owed for the re-send itself** (executor wording, ADR-0149 M1 note). Whether the "asked about after all" clause needs one follows from the seat's answer above.
- **SQL push-down: n/a.** No query, no id materialisation, no join in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md`** — step 1 holds against the matcher on `main`: a hit is equality after normalization and a candidate is containment either way, so "number of claims" equals the card's declared synonym where "claims" is only contained in it. One term per thing, the whole noun phrase, no translation or synonym, is what the matcher rewards. The dropped details (`matchedOn`, the candidate pointer shape, the "travel budget" pair) are not referred to anywhere else in the file. No sentence teaches a tool or a field the tools do not have.

**`dataset-next-step.ts`, `dataset-tools.ts`, `mcp-server-runtime.ts`** — the three texts agree with each other sentence by sentence, and the code places the sentence where the jsdoc says. One sentence of the jsdoc does not hold against the code: S1.

**S1 (should-fix) — the doors disagree on a re-sent phrase that matches nothing and has no candidate, and that path is the usual one, not a corner.**
- Three texts say the cut word is then asked about after all: the note, the description, the `initialize` rule. Eval case 25's `expected_output` says the same.
- Two say the opposite. (a) The answer to the re-send itself: `composeDatasetNextStep` reads that phrase as an unknown word and writes "equals no measure and has no possible reading. Answer with the object query tools…", with no question; the executor cannot know the call is a re-send. (b) The skill: its new sentence stops at "call `list_datasets` once more with the user's own phrase", it tells the reader to follow the answer's `decision` and `note`, and its own row says "No match and no candidates for the word for a thing measured: Step 4, without asking".
- So the jsdoc's "a re-sent phrase never turns a measure candidate into a labelled fallback" is not something the code does. It rests on the client holding the first note over the newer one.
- Why usual: a candidate is offered when a member's word CONTAINS the cut word. A longer phrase of the user's that is not itself a declared name, label or synonym is contained in nothing and usually contains nothing, so it comes back with no candidate.
- Effect: on the same question, a client that cut a word and re-sent the phrase ends in a question or in a labelled fallback depending on which text it follows; a client that sent the phrase first always ends in the fallback. No path selects a measure and no figure is wrong, which is why this is not a must-fix.
- Fix, one of two, after the seat's answer under ③: (A) keep "asked about after all" and say it in the skill's sentence too, with the jsdoc saying the client, not the executor, carries it; or (B) follow the amendment and rule 4: drop the clause from the three texts and from case 25, so a re-sent phrase with no candidate takes the labelled fallback everywhere.

**`evals/metric-selection-fallback.json`, case 25** — the prompt is the card's question, the expected first step (one more `list_datasets` call with "number of claims") is what the note orders, and `expected_output` passes its own assertions. Its last sentences depend on S1.

- **N1 (nit)** — case 25 does not forbid the reply it exists to prevent. Its `must_contain` is the tool name and the phrase; a reply that asks the user at once and names both passes. Cases 21 and 22 forbid the question's own words ("Do you mean", "do you mean"); the same two entries would close it.
- **N2 (nit)** — case 25 describes the note in its own words; cases 20, 21 and 24 quote the note as composed, which keeps a case honest when the copy moves.
- **N3 (nit)** — the skill's re-send sentence is tied to an answer that has `nextStep` ("a word it asks about"), and the unconditional sentence it replaces ("Ask only about matches or candidates for words the user wrote") is deleted. Every server on `main` sends `nextStep` when terms are sent, so nothing differs today.
- **N4 (nit)** — the note does not say whether the re-send carries the question's other terms. Case 25 re-sends both, which is the useful reading.

Does any sentence make an agent ask less where it must ask? One candidate only, S1's path (b), and there the alternative to the question is rule 4's labelled fallback, never a chosen measure. Does any sentence teach a behaviour the tools do not have? The jsdoc sentence quoted in S1; no sentence served to a client does.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-pe78f3`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c96d5bf9a11d9091b818acede64f1c14ee224a2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ask/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ask/evals/metric-selection-fallback.json + packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-next-step.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs
Security-touching: no

Delta review of record 7217619017 (head `5150e762`). Read: the one commit `7c96d5bf9a` on top of it (7 files, +21 / -22), the delta report 7218461224 on card #34996, and the check-runs on this head. `SKILL.md`, the generated copy and the ratchet row are byte-identical to the reviewed head; everything the first record judged outside this delta stands.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta removes one clause and adds no behaviour: right.** "…the word is asked about after all" is gone from `ownPhraseFirst` in `en`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW` and `ja-JP`, from `LIST_DATASETS_DESCRIPTION` and from `DATASET_SELECTION_RULE`. "Never the whole question" stays in all six. No code path moves: `composeDatasetNextStep` pushes the same sentence in the same two places, and `decision`, `terms`, `matches` and `candidates` are untouched.
- **The two pinning tests follow the text: right.** Both pin the shortened sentence; nothing else in them changes.
- **Check-runs on this head: 38 success, 18 skipped, 1 cancelled.** The cancelled one is a `PR-body guards` run superseded by a body edit; the same check concluded success on this head in a later run. No failure, nothing pending.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on the three packages, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset's first bullet now describes the head: the answer to the second call is followed like any other, and a phrase with no match and no candidate takes the labelled fallback.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The escalation of the first record is answered.** The seat chose B, which is the wording of claim amendment 7215005772 ("ask only if it still answers candidates"). The diff now says that and nothing more.
- **Inside ADR-0149 D3 as written.** A re-sent phrase with a measure among its candidates is asked about (the candidates note); one with no hit and no candidate takes rule 4's labelled fallback, which that note says is unchanged. No ADR note is owed: the delta leaves executor wording only (M1 note).
- **Delta report 7218461224: no open question.** Its deviation "this text has no eval round of its own" is noted, not judged: this record judges the text.
- **SQL push-down: n/a.**

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed

Every door now says the same thing about a re-sent phrase, and it is what the executor does:
- **The note, the description, the `initialize` rule**: re-send the phrase as written, never the whole question; no word about what follows.
- **The executor**: composes the second answer like any other. A measure candidate gives the question; no match and no candidate gives "Answer with the object query tools…".
- **The jsdoc**: says exactly that, and that this file cannot know a call is a re-send. The sentence the first record found untrue is gone.
- **The skill**: "call `list_datasets` once more with the user's own phrase", then follow the answer's `decision` and `note`; its row "No match and no candidates … Step 4, without asking" is now the same instruction as the second answer's note.
- **Eval case 25**: `expected_output` names the three outcomes of the second call (one measure computed, a measure candidate asked about, no match and no candidate answered by the object tools with the not-governed line). It passes its own assertions.

A client that cut a word and re-sent the phrase now ends where a client that sent the phrase first ends. No text makes an agent ask less than D3 requires: the question is still owed for the user's own word and for a re-sent phrase that keeps a measure candidate, and no text selects a candidate.

Nits of the first record:
- N1: closed. Case 25 forbids "Do you mean" and "do you mean".
- N2: closed. Case 25 quotes the note; read against `COPY.en` and the composer's order for `['claims', 'status']` (asked word, re-send sentence, conditioned question, possible grouping, its tail), the quote is the composed text.
- N3, N4: left as accepted deviations (nits, no effect on the contract).

Nothing new in the delta. No must-fix, no should-fix.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 7c96d5bf9a · card #34996 · area s2-eval · 2026-11-27T12:39Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and checks.** 38 success, 18 expected skip on the head; the one `cancelled` PR-body guards run was superseded by the body edit and the same check is success on this head in a later run. Draft, mergeable clean.
- **Contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`.** 7217619017 at `5150e762`: PASS with S1 open (the texts said a re-sent phrase with no match and no candidate is asked about; the executor and the skill take rule 4's labelled fallback). The seat chose fix B, which keeps ADR-0149 D3 rule 4 and claim amendment 7215005772 as written. The delta record 7218502316 at this head: `S1: closed`, N1 and N2 closed, `No must-fix, no should-fix.`; N3 and N4 accepted as deviations. The transcript passes `verify-review-tier`. The seat adopts them.
- **What changes for an agent.** When the data agent's question has a word it shortened or reworded, it re-checks the user's own phrase once (never the whole question) before asking; a measure candidate is still asked, never chosen; `matches`, `candidates`, `decision` and the D3 rules are untouched.
- **Evidence, stated as it is.** haiku/medium, travel_expense, 5 runs each, 65 ask points: baseline 61; r2 63, r3 64, r4 (r3's tree) 59; pooled 95.4% against 91.5%. One direction, inside run-to-run spread. This head's text sits between r2 and r3 and has no round of its own; the maintainer chose to pause further runs. The card's target (two consecutive rounds) is not met, so `Part of #34996` is right and the card stays open. The keep rule's weakness is #37921.
- **Budget and declarations.** `skills/objectstack-ask` net +10 lines (budget +25), the token ratchet row lowered 1875 → 1873, no ceiling raised; `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, three packages at `patch`.
- **Governance.** `skills/**`: Tier H. The maintainer's approval lands it.

Tier: H. Landing: hand-off to the maintainer follows this record.

## 维护者速读
- **改了什么：** 问数技能和数据集工具的说明里加一条：用户问题里的词被截短或改写过时，先用用户原话里的那个词组重查一次（不是整句问题），再决定要不要反问。只改技能文字、工具说明和下一步提示语（四种语言），匹配、候选和决策规则都没动；有指标候选仍然只问不选。
- **影响：** 数据 Agent 少问一些不必要的反问。评测（haiku/medium，旅行报销，每轮 5 次，满分 65）：基线 61，改后 63、64，同一棵树复测 59；合并看 95.4% 对 91.5%，方向一致，但没有超出轮间波动。这是弱证据，你 11:36Z 选了先交现有 PR、暂停加跑。卡的目标（连续两轮达标）没达到，所以写的是 `Part of #34996`，卡不关。
- **请你留意：** 技能目录走 Tier H。保留判据本身分辨不了这么小的改动，另立卡 #37921。
- **审核：** 契约审核（最高档）第一轮 PASS 但有一处建议改（说明里一句话和工具实际行为相反），按与 ADR-0149 规则 4 一致的方案修了，增量复审 PASS（7218502316），没有必须改或建议改的项。席位 L1 ACCEPT 在本评论前一条。
- **要你做什么：** 需要你批准后才能合并。撤回这一次合并即恢复原样。
